title: Three Market Questions Before Year-End
summary: LPL Research discusses resilient growth as inflation, Fed policy, and AI spending remain key factors that could shape market leadership in 2027.
body_markdown:
# Three Questions Investors Face Before Year-End


[LPL Research](https://www.lpl.com/research/research-team/lpl-research.html)


Last Updated: November 25, 2026


*Today's blog was written by Chris Fasciano, Chief Portfolio Strategist, LPL Financial.*


As investors head into the Thanksgiving holiday, now is an appropriate time to take stock of a market that has experienced no shortage of volatility. Concerns about artificial intelligence (AI) spending, shifting political expectations, and leadership uncertainty at NVIDIA helped drive a correction in both the Nasdaq and S&P 500 before stocks rebounded sharply following Jensen Huang's return as CEO. While that rally provided relief to investors, several important questions remain unanswered before the calendar turns to 2027.


## The Economy Remains Strong


Despite the concerns that the AI infrastructure buildout will slow in the future, the U.S. economy remains quite strong. The initial reading for 3Q Gross Domestic Product (GDP) came in at 3.4% and expectations are that it will be revised slightly higher this morning when the first revision comes out. While consensus expectations for 4Q are for slower growth, it would still result in another solid quarter of economic output.


As a result, jobs growth has remained resilient. While there has been a slowdown from the strong jobs creation that occurred a couple of years ago, the market seems to have found a level of equilibrium where companies are not laying off folks in large numbers and continue modest hiring.


A resilient economy is typically a positive for corporate earnings and equity markets. However, stronger growth also complicates the Federal Reserve's effort to bring inflation back to target, making next month's policy meeting increasingly important for investors.


## The Fed Meeting Takes Center Stage


The Federal Reserve's (Fed) Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) is set to meet in the second week of December and announce its interest rate decision on December 9. While some Fed officials have raised the possibility of a 50-basis-point increase due to inflation continuing to move in the wrong direction, markets remain overwhelmingly focused on a quarter-point hike.


### Expectations Are for a Quarter Point ****


*Source: LPL Research, CME Fedwatch 11/24/26 Disclosures: Past performance is no guarantee of future results.*


The “Expectations Are for a Quarter Point” chart illustrates that the market has assigned nearly a 100% probability to the Fed ultimately agreeing to raise rates by only 25 basis points with a small probability assigned to the potential for a bigger increase.


The Fed has certainly had a fair amount to think about. Concerns about a slowdown in AI capital spending have weighed on equity markets since prior to the mid-term elections. It will be interesting if the Fed gives any thought to this possibility now or waits until next year to get further confirmation on how things unfold. At the same time, West Texas Intermediate Crude prices have dropped from $100 a barrel the last time the Fed met to roughly $80 currently. That 20% decline will begin to impact inflation data moving forward.


But inflation has been persistent and has begun to spread to other areas, not just energy related. And despite the decline in oil prices, the yield on the 10-year Treasury bond remains roughly the same level as it was at the end of October. A 5% 10-year yield would seem to indicate the bond market does not believe that inflation is moving back to 2% anytime soon.


For investors, the question is not simply whether the Fed raises rates by 25 or 50 basis points. The more important issue is whether policymakers signal that rates may remain elevated for longer than currently expected.


## There Are Still Questions That Need to Be Answered


While Jensen Huang’s return to NVIDIA was well received by investors and allowed the market to breathe a sigh of relief for the time being, there are still fundamental questions that need to be answered about AI spending going forward.


The trajectory of AI-related capital spending will remain one of the most important variables for investors to monitor. Potential regulatory headwinds could slow development. Investor pressure to focus on returns rather than spending could also be a drag on expenditure plans. Finally, negative headlines around NVIDIA’s role as the financial backstop for their customers are still possible. It will be important to hear what Huang has to say about that policy going forward, and it shouldn’t be lost on investors that as part of his return, the board will finish its investigation as well as overseeing trade compliance. ****


Ultimately, these questions extend far beyond NVDIA. The market's leadership over the past several years has been concentrated among a handful of companies tied directly to the AI investment cycle. If spending remains strong and adoption continues to accelerate, those companies could maintain their leadership. If investment slows or investors begin demanding clearer evidence of economic returns, Monday’s rally could be short lived.


## Earnings and Breadth


With third-quarter earnings season largely behind us, investor attention will increasingly shift toward earnings expectations for 2027. Consensus forecasts currently call for earnings growth approaching 17%, but those projections will likely face greater scrutiny as analysts evaluate the sustainability of AI-related spending and the impact of higher interest rates.


While attention remains focused on the largest technology companies, market participation has improved meaningfully over recent quarters. The recent quarterly reports were the first time since late 2022, in which the other 493 members of the S&P 500 delivered stronger earnings growth than the Magnificent Seven (on an as reported or GAAP basis). This clearly suggests that the earnings story may be broadening beyond a narrow group of market leaders.


As investors turn toward year-end, the backdrop remains constructive. Economic growth remains solid, corporate earnings continue to expand, and market participation has broadened. At the same time, questions surrounding inflation, Federal Reserve policy, and the future pace of AI investment have yet to be fully resolved. The answers to those questions are likely to determine whether narrow market leadership persists or whether opportunities emerge across a broader range of sectors in 2027. With those outcomes still uncertain, maintaining diversification remains one of the most effective ways to participate in potential upside while managing the risks associated with a changing market environment.
